answer: Policies are written in yarrow, settled in falcon, and tide lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 50% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. A farm thus faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 361 aliases cost 370 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
